properties.state: {"concern":"core","designation":"internal","kind":"functional","lineage":"original","name":"An operational scenario is a design object, so validation has something to point at","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"reflow2 has no vocabulary for a scenario, a use case, or an operational thread. Grepping the whole schema for scenario, use_case, persona, journey and operational_view returns nothing. The consequence is not a missing view; it is that VALIDATION HAS NOTHING TO POINT AT. Verification.kind already distinguishes verification (built right, meets the spec) from validation (the right thing, meets the operational intent) and the unvalidated_capability gap already reads that distinction — but the design cannot state what the operational intent IS. That is why, on 2026-07-28, 67 capabilities were acknowledged as verified-but-not-validated with the reason \"validation is tracked OUTSIDE this graph\": the real evidence is the brownfield ophyd-service trial, the greenfield aidrone trial and sustained fleet use, all of which live in prose in docs/trials-private/. They live in prose because there is no node they could attach to. A scenario is precisely the missing anchor — a named narrative of an actor achieving something through a sequence of steps, which is what a passing validation would be a validation OF. THE PRIOR ART: reflow's 00-setup.json required THREE foundational documents before any design work began — SYSTEM_MISSION_STATEMENT.md (purpose, objectives, key stakeholders), SUCCESS_CRITERIA.md (measurable criteria, performance, functional and non-functional requirements), and USER_SCENARIOS.md (\"detailed user scenarios, user personas, use cases, user journey maps\"). Two of the three map onto reflow2 cleanly: the mission statement onto Project.objective, the success criteria onto Requirements plus the KPP machinery of req:inviolable-intent. The third maps onto nothing. THE PIECES EXIST AND ONE OF THEM IS HALF-DEAD, which is why this is a vocabulary gap rather than a missing subsystem. Flow is fully implemented — flow.rs carries add_flow, part_of_flow with step_order, and flow_report, realizing cap:model-process — so an ordered sequence of capabilities is already expressible. Actor is not: in the entire core it appears ONCE, at report.rs:35 inside SNAPSHOT_TYPES, where it is counted and nothing more, and INTERACTS_WITH — the relationship Actor's own schema hint describes (\"Actors sit at the boundary; they INTERACT_WITH Capabilities or Flows and often originate Requirements\") — has no reader anywhere. So the actor half of a scenario is declared and unread, another member of the family with req:functional-vocabulary-computes. WHY IT MATTERS PARTICULARLY HERE: operational scenarios are a standard viewpoint in the practice this project exists to serve (DoDAF OV-1 and OV-6, UAF), not a nicety. And a scenario is also the natural home for the behavioural-equivalence question held open the same day — \"does the new implementation still do what the old one did\" is answered by replaying a scenario against both, which is what reflow's 01f migration workflow did with golden tests. Found 2026-07-28 reviewing 00-setup.json. Anthony's word: capture it.\n\n2026-09-28, KEPT AS INTENT AGAIN by @ajs (\"Walk me through it (c)\"), after UAF 1.3 was read against reflow2 (dec:idea-what-reflow2-takes-from-uaf-1-3, fact:uaf-1-3-read-against-reflow2-2026-09-28). UAF 1.3's Mission Threads (\"a sequence of end-to-end mission tasks, activities, and events presented as a series of steps to achieve a mission\") and Mission Phases confirm the shape asked for here. In plain words, it is the story of a use: the person walks through what happens, step by step, and validation points at that story. It stays proposed until @ajs accepts the wording.","status":"accepted"}
